title: Upper-intermediate Grammar (Essential Grammar in Use - Murphy)
lesson_overview: B2 level covers nuanced structures for confident communication in complex contexts, including mixed conditionals and advanced modals.

topics.name: Mixed Conditionals
topics.lesson_text: Mixed conditionals combine different time references in the if-clause and main clause. Present result of past condition: If I had accepted that job, I would be living in London now. Past result of present condition: If I knew his number, I would have called him yesterday. Structure: if + past perfect, would + base verb (present result). if + present, would have + past participle (past result). Also: unless, as long as, in case with mixed meanings. Note: Not all mixed conditional combinations are equally common; some sound more natural than others.
examples: If I had taken that job, I would be living in London now.
If I knew his number, I would have called him yesterday.
If she hadn't missed the train, she would be here by now.

topics.name: Inversion
topics.focus: Not only, hardly/scarce, so rare a...that
topics.lesson_text: Inverted word order after negative adverbs/expressions for emphasis. After 'not only': 'Not only + auxiliary verb + subject + main verb, but also...'. After 'hardly/scarce/barely': 'Hardly + auxiliary + subject + when/than + clause'. After 'so + a/an + adjective + singular countable noun': 'So rare a student that...'. Other expressions: 'at no time', 'on no condition', 'under no circumstances'. Normal order: I have never seen him. Inverted: Never have I seen him. Note: Inversion is formal style, common in written English, especially literature and journalism.
examples: Not only he came, but also his brother.
Hardly had I arrived when the phone rang.
So exhausted was he that he could not walk.

topics.name: Subjunctive
topics.focus: It's time, as if/as though, wish
topics.lesson_text: Subjunctive mood expresses wishes, hypotheses, demands, suggestions. 'It's time' + past simple for present/future: It's time you went. 'I wish' + past simple/past perfect for present/unreal: I wish I spoke French. 'As if/as though' + past simple for imagined present: He looks as if he knew the answer. 'Would rather' + past simple for preference: I'd rather you went now. Note: Past form of 'be' is 'were' for all persons in subjunctive: If I were you. 'Wish' with would for annoying habit: I wish he would stop smoking.
examples: It's time you went to bed.
I wish I had more free time.
He looks as if he knew the answer.

topics.name: Advanced Modals
topics.focus: might, should, ought to, had better
topics.lesson_text: Might: weaker possibility than could/may, reported speech past of can: He said he might come. Should: advice, recommendation, logical deduction: You should see a doctor. Ought to: similar to should, slightly more formal, moral obligation. Had better: strong advice for specific situation, negative consequence: You had better study or you'll fail. Needn't: not necessary (no need to). Must vs have to: must = personal obligation, have to = external requirement. Note: Ought to + base verb, not 'to'. Had better + base verb (no 'to'). Negative: hadn't better or you'll regret it.
examples: You had better hurry or you'll be late.

cefr_description: Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible.
